Heritage walk in Prayagraj: Sangam, Khusro Bagh and the colonial city

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) takes in the Sangam of the Ganga and Yamuna, Akbar's fort with the Ashokan pillar inside, the Mughal tombs of Khusro Bagh, the colonial Civil Lines with All Saints Cathedral and the university, Anand Bhavan and the Allahabad Museum. Kaushambi, an early historic city, is about 60 km away.

We arrange Prayagraj heritage walks and study tours on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Prayagraj matters

Prayagraj stands at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, a place of pilgrimage described in early texts and the site of the Kumbh Mela. Akbar founded a fortified city here in the 1570s and 1580s, naming it Ilahabas, later Allahabad. The city was renamed Prayagraj in 2018.

It is also central to modern Indian history. The East India Company's rule passed to the Crown by a proclamation read here in 1858, the city was capital of the North-Western Provinces and later the United Provinces, and it was a political and intellectual centre of the freedom movement, home to the Nehru family and to one of India's oldest universities.

Layers of Prayagraj's history

The oldest standing object in the city is the Ashokan pillar inside the fort, of the 3rd century BCE. It carries Ashoka's edicts and, later, Samudragupta's long Prayaga Prashasti of the 4th century CE, written by his court poet Harishena, and a Persian inscription of Jahangir. It was probably brought here from Kaushambi, the capital of the Vatsa mahajanapada, about 60 km away, where excavations have found city walls and early historic layers. The Gupta Empire and Ashoka and his edicts guides explain both inscriptions.

Akbar's fort, begun in 1583, still dominates the Sangam; much of it is in army use. Khusro Bagh holds the tombs of Jahangir's son Khusrau (died 1622), his mother Shah Begum and his sister, with fine Mughal painted and carved work.

After 1857 the British built the Civil Lines on a grid, with All Saints Cathedral (1871 onward) by William Emerson, Muir College (now part of Allahabad University, founded 1887) and the High Court. Anand Bhavan and Swaraj Bhavan, the Nehru family homes, became centres of the Congress movement. Chandra Shekhar Azad died in Alfred Park (now Chandra Shekhar Azad Park) in 1931.

Places a heritage walk in Prayagraj covers

  1. Triveni Sangam ancient tirtha

    Confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, seen best from a boat; the site of the Kumbh Mela.

  2. Allahabad Fort 1583 onward

    Akbar's riverside fort, largely in army use; see the walls from the river.

  3. Ashokan Pillar 3rd century BCE, later inscriptions

    Pillar inside the fort with edicts of Ashoka, Samudragupta's prashasti and a Jahangir inscription.

  4. Khusro Bagh 1620s

    Walled garden with the tombs of Prince Khusrau, Shah Begum and Sultan Nithar Begum.

  5. All Saints Cathedral 1871 to 1887

    Gothic revival cathedral by William Emerson in Civil Lines.

  6. Muir College 1873 to 1886

    Indo-Saracenic college building by William Emerson, now part of Allahabad University.

  7. Allahabad High Court 1916 building

    Large court building of the High Court, established in 1866.

  8. Chandra Shekhar Azad Park laid out 1870

    Former Alfred Park, where Azad died in 1931; houses the Allahabad Museum and the Thornhill Mayne Memorial.

  9. Thornhill Mayne Memorial 1878

    Gothic public library building in the park.

  10. Anand Bhavan 1930

    Nehru family home given over to the nation, with rooms kept as they were.

  11. Swaraj Bhavan older house, donated 1930

    Earlier Nehru home that became the Congress headquarters.

  12. Kaushambi early first millennium BCE onward

    Ancient Vatsa capital about 60 km away, with city walls and excavated mounds.

Walking routes in Prayagraj

Civil Lines and the park on foot

About 3 hours

All Saints Cathedral → Allahabad High Court → Chandra Shekhar Azad Park → Thornhill Mayne Memorial → Muir College

Nehru homes and Khusro Bagh

About 3 hours, short drive between

Anand Bhavan → Swaraj Bhavan → Khusro Bagh

Sangam and the fort

Half a day, by vehicle and boat

Triveni Sangam → Allahabad Fort → Ashokan Pillar

Museums in Prayagraj

  • Allahabad Museum. Sculpture and terracotta from Kaushambi and Bharhut, coins, miniature paintings and freedom movement material.
  • Anand Bhavan. House museum of the Nehru family and the Congress movement, with a planetarium next door.

Best time for a walk

October to March, avoiding the weeks of the Kumbh or Magh Mela for school groups.

What you see on a walk

At Khusro Bagh, students compare three Mughal tombs in one garden and look closely at painted ceilings and carved stone. In Civil Lines they see a planned colonial grid with Gothic and Indo-Saracenic buildings. At Anand Bhavan they see how a house became a political headquarters.

The pillar's inscriptions make Prayagraj an excellent place to introduce India's scripts from Brahmi to Sarada or a hands-on Brahmi workshop. The Allahabad Museum's sculpture and terracotta from Kaushambi suit Reading sculpture.

Prayagraj for school and college groups

Prayagraj visits are planned as a study tour built for your group, often combined with Varanasi, Sarnath or Kaushambi.

Civil Lines, the museum, Chandra Shekhar Azad Park and Anand Bhavan are close together and walkable. Khusro Bagh is in the old city and the Sangam and fort are to the south-east; use a vehicle between them. Access inside the fort is restricted because of army use, and the pillar may not always be open to visitors, so check in advance. During the Kumbh and Magh Mela the Sangam area is very crowded and not suitable for school groups.

How we run this

  • Schools: a Brahmi workshop in class, then a Prayagraj study day on Ashoka, the Guptas and the freedom movement.
  • Colleges: Kaushambi and the Allahabad Museum for early historic archaeology.
  • Families: Khusro Bagh and Civil Lines with a historian.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Prayagraj?

The Sangam, Akbar's fort with the Ashokan pillar, Khusro Bagh, All Saints Cathedral, Muir College, the High Court, Chandra Shekhar Azad Park, Anand Bhavan, Swaraj Bhavan and the Allahabad Museum. Kaushambi is a day trip.

What is written on the Allahabad pillar?

Edicts of Ashoka from the 3rd century BCE, the Prayaga Prashasti of the Gupta king Samudragupta from the 4th century CE, and a Persian inscription of Jahangir.

Is a Prayagraj heritage walk good for schools?

Yes. Civil Lines, the museum and Anand Bhavan are close together and easy to manage. Avoid the Sangam during the Kumbh or Magh Mela, and check access to the fort in advance.

Which museums are in Prayagraj?

The Allahabad Museum in Chandra Shekhar Azad Park, with strong archaeology and painting collections, and Anand Bhavan, the Nehru house museum.

Can Talaash Heritage arrange a Prayagraj study tour?

Yes, on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, often combined with Varanasi and Kaushambi.
